_comments: Sample configuration for Google Spanner with the PostgreSQL interface (EXPERIMENTAL - not yet verified end-to-end).
Two connection options are provided below. Option B (PGAdapter + pgjdbc) is recommended
as it uses the same PostgreSQL JDBC driver as all other PostgreSQL-family databases,
and is fully compatible with orm_skyway's UUID support.
=== OPTION B (Recommended): PGAdapter + standard PostgreSQL JDBC driver ===
Step 1: Pull and start the combined PGAdapter + Spanner emulator Docker container (Windows):
docker pull gcr.io/cloud-spanner-pg-adapter/pgadapter-emulator
docker run -d -p 5432:5432 -p 9010:9010 -p 9020:9020 gcr.io/cloud-spanner-pg-adapter/pgadapter-emulator
No Google Cloud credentials, gcloud CLI, or separate JRE needed.
Any database name you connect to is auto-created.
Data is in-memory only -- all state is lost when the container stops.
Step 2: Use this config with the Option B settings below.
jdbc_url points to PGAdapter on localhost:5432 using standard pgjdbc (42.0.0+).
The postgresql-42.2.29.jar already bundled in the Gilhari SDK works.
Spanner-specific schema notes:
- Every table must have an explicit PRIMARY KEY (no implicit rowid)
- SERIAL is not supported -- use BIGINT, VARCHAR, or UUID with gen_random_uuid()
- Foreign key constraints are not enforced by the local emulator
- See https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/postgresql/data-definition-language
=== OPTION A (Fallback): Spanner JDBC driver directly ===
Uncomment the Option A settings and comment out Option B.
Download the Spanner JDBC driver from https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/jdbc-drivers
Copy to your project root, rename to orm_skyway_config.json, and edit for your database.
Run: python orm_skyway.py -f orm_skyway_config.json --phase 1+3
_option_a_fallback: Spanner JDBC driver directly (uncomment and comment out Option B above)
